business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Physical Arbitrage of Grade A Refined Copper Cathodes

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (federal unitary commercial law; cantonal administrative autonomy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Swiss BIT network: over 120 Bilateral Investment Treaties in force, including China, India, Russia, Brazil, UAE and major raw-material producing states
Swiss DTA network: over 100 Double Taxation Agreements in force, including with all G20/OECD jurisdictions and metals-trading hubs such as Singapore, UAE, Kazakhstan and China
EFTA–China Free Trade Agreement (entered into force 1 July 2014; applicable to Switzerland as an EFTA member)
EFTA–GCC Free Trade Agreement (relevant to Gulf copper and non-ferrous metals trade)
Bilateral Investment Treaty protections applied on a UBO-by-UBO basis according to the composite UBO matrix at onboarding

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0), 10 October 1997 as amended, in particular Arts. 4, 6 and 8-9; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Arts. 305bis, 305ter and 260ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Arts. 627, 697i and 697j (share register, bearer shares and disclosure of ultimate owners); Federal Act and Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV, SR 221.411); Federal Act on Embargoes (SR 946.231) and SECO-implementing ordinances; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA) to the extent the opening bank/fiduciary is a financial intermediary; Federal Act on the Protection of the Swiss Cross and Swissness Act (SR 232.21) for name clearance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official commercial register extract / certificate of good standing of each corporate shareholder and ultimate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Switzerland) or competent corporate registry in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the issuing jurisdiction is party to the 1961 Hague Convention); otherwise Consular Legalization by the Swiss representation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized statutes/memorandum and articles of association of each corporate UBO and, if applicable, each intermediate holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or notary in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency / share register / UBO certificate confirming the natural persons owning or controlling the shareholder chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent, fiduciary, corporate registry, or legal counsel in the UBO's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized/certified passport copies of all directors, officers and natural-person beneficial owners with a direct or indirect interest of 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority (notarized/certified by a notary public or embassy in country of origin)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available; otherwise notarized certification accepted under Swiss KYC practice and AMLA Art. 6

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for the Swiss incorporation signatories and registered agent, if the shareholders will not sign the deed personally
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), Arts. 620–761 (Aktiengesellschaft), notably Arts. 626–631 (incorporation, share capital, paid-up requirements) and Art. 640 (Board of Directors); Art. 715 (signature authority); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV) Arts. 4, 8, 10 and 64.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce), acting under the supervision of the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt, EHRA) within the Federal Office for the Civil Registry (Bundesamt für Zivilstandswesen).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised Public Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde mit Statuten) filed as the official registration application with the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zum Handelsregister).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital is CHF 100,000 nominal; at least 20% (CHF 20,000) must be fully paid up in cash before registration. The paid-up contribution must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) held with a FINMA-regulated Swiss bank, and a bank confirmation of capital availability (Kapitaleinzahlungsbestätigung) must be submitted to the notary and the Commercial Register. Contributions in kind require an audit confirmatory report (Sachgründungsbericht).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers’ share subscription and payment declarations are approved, and that the Company, incorporated as an Aktiengesellschaft under the name [Company Name] AG, with registered office in Zurich, is hereby ratified and constituted; RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office is established at [Corporate Address], Canton of Zurich; RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name], [Name] and [Name] are appointed as members of the Board of Directors, with [Name] as Chairperson, each to serve until the next Annual General Meeting; RESOLVED FURTHER that individual or joint signature authority is granted to [Name] and [Name] in accordance with the articles; RESOLVED FINALLY that the Board is authorised to execute all filings with the Commercial Register Office and the Swiss Federal Tax Administration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) / Federal Commercial Register Central Name Database (ZEFIX)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance request via the cantonal Commercial Register Office or an authorised notary. The name must include 'AG' or 'SA', must not be misleading, and must not infringe existing trademarks or registered company names. Reserve the exact corporate name ('[Company Name] AG') and obtain a preliminary name clearance certificate before notarisation.
required_dossiers: Duly completed name clearance request form
Identity documents of the applicant/founder
Proposed articles of association draft (name clause)
Declaration of absence of third-party rights to the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, modify the name with a distinct element (geographical or descriptive suffix), address any misleading-capacity objection raised by the Registrar, and resubmit the clearance application; internal appeal to the cantonal Commercial Register Office is available within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (öffentlicher Notar / Notaire public) acting under cantonal supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the founders at the notary’s office. The notary certifies the deed of incorporation, the articles of association (Statutes), and the declaration that all shares have been subscribed. Articles must include corporate purpose (wholesale trading of non-ferrous metals), registered seat, share capital, par value of shares, board rules, and authorised signature clauses. The notary then registers the deed for the subsequent Commercial Register filing.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or Swiss ID of each founder/shareholder
Draft articles of association (Four-language model optional: DE/FR/IT/EN)
Name clearance certificate
Subscription declaration forms for all shares
Payment declaration and schedule for subscribed capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, amend and re-execute the deed; any missing cantonal formality is cured by supplementary notarial certification before the registration application proceeds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution and Blocked Account Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-regulated Swiss bank (Sperrkonto / bloqué account) and Swiss audit/licensing body for confirmatory report
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the company name (pre-registration account) and transfer the cash share capital of at least CHF 20,000. Obtain an unconditional bank confirmation (Kapitaleinzahlungsbestätigung) stating the amount is at the free disposal of the incorporators subject only to the Commercial Register registration. If contributions in kind are used, obtain a statutory contribution-in-kind report (Sachgründungsbericht).
required_dossiers: Bank confirmation form (provided by the chosen Swiss bank)
Copy of incorporation deed and articles
Individual payment instructions or wire transfer receipt
In-kind contribution valuation report (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening or the confirmation is non-conforming, rectify the payment documentation or choose an alternative FINMA-regulated bank; the notary must be informed of any change in the capital payment mechanism.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) in the canton of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the duly notarised deed, articles, bank capital confirmation, and board resolution to the Commercial Register Office via the notary. The filing is made on the official form (Anmeldung/Form 105.1) signed by all board members. The office verifies legal compliance, representation, and paid-up capital. Upon approval, the company is legally incorporated and the registration data is forwarded for publication.
required_dossiers: Notarised deed of incorporation (original)
Notarised articles of association (certified copy)
Bank capital payment confirmation
Signed board resolution appointing directors and officers
Specimen signature cards or electronic signature registers for signatories
Completed Anmeldung zum Handelsregister form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an objection or request for clarification, respond with supplementary documents within the statutory deadline (usually 10 days); an appeal against refusal lies with the competent cantonal court (Verwaltungsgericht) within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB) operated by the Federal Department of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Cantonal Commercial Register entry, the SHAB publication is automatically initiated by the registrar. Publication contains company name, seat, purpose, capital, officers, and signature rules. The company becomes legally effective vis-à-vis third parties from the SHAB publication date; review the published text for accuracy.
required_dossiers: No separate filing – Commercial Register entry generates the SHAB notice
Company registration extract (Handelsregisterauszug) for verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published data contains an error, file a correction request with the Commercial Register Office within 30 days; any third-party reliance loss may be remedied via a corrective republication at the registrar's direction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Social Insurance, and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA – Main Division VAT), Cantonal Tax Office, and relevant compensation fund (SUVA/SVA) and AHV-Ausgleichskasse
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for VAT if annual taxable worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 (compulsory); voluntary VAT registration is possible for non-income-generating companies. Also register as employer with the AHV compensation office (for salaries, AHV/UV/EO contributions), and for professional accident insurance with SUVA. File the corporate income tax registration form with the cantonal tax office within 60 days of incorporation to obtain the cantonal and federal tax numbers.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract dated within 30 days
VAT registration form (Formulaire 119 / 120)
Articles of incorporation and deed
Bank account details
Employer registration form (for payroll and social security)
Cantonal tax registration questionnaire (state/local tax purposes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is queried, provide the estimated turnover calculation and supporting evidence of business activity; for social insurance, cooperate with the compensation fund to retroactively register employees and remedy any contribution gaps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open LME-Warrant and Documentary LC Banking Arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-regulated Swiss bank corporate desk; self-regulatory compliance function (Verein gegen Geldwäscherei / Banking Ombudsman framework)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account and negotiate documentary letter of credit (LC) lines and LME warrant transfer capabilities with the bank’s commodity finance desk. Submit corporate due diligence package, business plan, AML risk assessment, sanctions screening (copper cathode sourcing), and board resolution authorising the account. Confirm the bank’s ability to handle LME warrant transfers and UCP 600 documentary collections.
required_dossiers: Incorporation documents and Commercial Register extract
Certificate of beneficial ownership and identification of UBOs
Board resolution approving bank account and authorised signatories
Business plan and projected commodity trading volumes
AML/KYC questionnaire and sanctions compliance statement
Sourcing and due diligence policy for physical copper cathodes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank demands additional KYC documentation, supply enhanced UBO declarations, side letters, or an audit opinion; if sanctions screening flags the counterparty, provide proof of jurisdiction and end-user compliance before the bank releases payment controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade and Industry Inspectorate (Kantonales Gewerbeinspektorat / Inspection cantonale du commerce) and SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) for core wholesale trading; no manufacturing industrial licence required under the Trade Act (BBG/SEC) because the scope is limited to wholesale physical arbitrage of refined copper cathodes.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Wholesale wholesale trading requires no sectoral industrial permit in Switzerland; merely a general business registration declaration (Anmeldung) via the Commercial Register. If incidental storage/warehousing of copper cathodes is operated, a cantonal storage-activity registration and building-use authorisation may be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN), acting through the cantonal environmental protection authority (Amt für Umwelt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not subject to a full EIA (UVPV/OEIE Annex list does not cover wholesale trading of metals). Depending on storage scale, a simplified cantonal plant registration or preliminary environmental assessment may be requested; office-only use is exempt.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds: zero process wastewater discharge for pure trading; if storage occurs, rainwater runoff must meet the requirements of the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV, SR 814.201). Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) not relevant from cathodes; the VOC Ordinance (SR 814.018) remains applicable to any ancillary solvent use. Waste handling, including packaging and scrap, must comply with the Waste Ordinance (VVEA, SR 814.600), requiring e.g. segregation and recycling certificates. Cathode storage areas must be contained against dust dispersion and meet BAFU ambient air thresholds (PM10) under the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV, SR 814.318.142.1).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the cantonal fire prevention authority (AICAA / Gebäudeversicherung): fire alarm and extinguisher systems, emergency exits, and storage separation distances per VKF/AEAI norms. Structural load inspection for any racking and cathode storage floors per SIA 260 and SIA 263 standards, with load-bearing capacity report. Occupational safety clearance under the Labour Act (ArG, SR 822.11) and SUVA guidelines: first-aid equipment, lifting/manual-handling protocols, operator instruction, and an internal occupational safety and health plan; employees working with heavy cathode bundles require edge protection and PPE compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Bundesgasse 32, 3003 Bern; e-filing portal: www.estv.admin.ch; UID register portal: www.uid.admin.ch. Cantonal and communal tax authorities assess corporate income and capital taxes jointly with the Confederation, while the ESTV has sole competence for VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss-incorporated Aktiengesellschaft is automatically entered in the national UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) register upon Commercial Register enrollment; the issued UID concurrently functions as the VAT identification number. For VAT-specific activation, the AG or its Swiss attorney submits the ESTV Form 001 (registration sheet for taxable persons) with a current Commercial Register extract to the ESTV VAT Division; VAT registration becomes legally effective upon ESTV written confirmation. Registration is mandatory for Swiss-resident entities once worldwide turnover from taxable supplies exceeds CHF 100,000 per calendar year, and voluntary registration below the threshold is available under Art. 11 of the VAT Act. A foreign-owned trading AG must appoint a Swiss tax representative with domestic service address for VAT procedural purposes, but no statutory license is required for wholesale base-metals trading.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – A Swiss AG is a separate legal taxpayer, subject to unlimited corporate income tax liability on worldwide profits with carve-outs for foreign permanent establishments and immovable property; no pass-through or look-through treatment applies. Federal corporate income tax is levied at the effective statutory rate of 8.5% after federal surtax mechanics, plus cantonal/municipal profit tax and capital tax; profit allocation follows arm's length substance principles for commodity traders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not provide check-the-box or pass-through classification elections. Relevant statutory elections for the AG: (i) VAT group taxation under Art. 62 VAT Act for closely connected entities; (ii) voluntary VAT registration below CHF 100,000 turnover under Art. 11 VAT Act; (iii) election of monthly VAT filing instead of quarterly filing; (iv) participation exemption relief for dividend income under Art. 70 of the Federal Direct Tax Act (not an elective regime); and (v) advance tax rulings with the cantonal tax administration confirming profit attribution, warehouse permanent establishment treatment, or margin recognition for offshore copper trades. Swiss domestic rules implementing OECD BEPS Action 2 neutralize hybrid mismatches without elective deductions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / Imposta sul valore aggiunto) governed by the Swiss VAT Act of 12 June 2009, effective 1 January 2010; a credit-invoice VAT system with input tax deduction and no separate GST or cantonal sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (Art. 10 para. 2 lit. a VAT Act). Swiss-resident AGs with turnover below CHF 100,000 are exempt unless they opt in under Art. 11. For supplies of goods physically located in Switzerland, including consignment stock of non-ferrous copper cathodes, the supplier must register once turnover exceeds the threshold; the import of copper cathodes into Swiss customs territory by the AG also triggers VAT at the border. Purely offshore back-to-back trades where the goods never enter Swiss territory are outside the Swiss VAT territorial scope and confer no Swiss creditable input tax on VAT-bearing costs unless tied to taxable Swiss supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no approved-invoice software mandate, no digital fiscal stamp, and no mandatory clearance API. VAT accounting is executed through periodic returns submitted on the official ESTV VAT portal (quarterly by default; semi-annual below CHF 5,000,000 turnover; monthly optional), integrating tax due and deductible input tax. The Swiss eBill standard, Peppol-compliant EDI flows, and scanned paper invoices are accepted as documentary records; invoices must comply with Art. 26 VAT Act (supplier UID, recipient, date, nature of supply, consideration, rate, and separately stated tax). Books and records must be retained for ten years, and the ESTV may conduct remote digital audits without prior notice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Art. 23 para. 1 VAT Act, the delivery of movable goods is zero-rated when the supplier or a commissioned carrier dispatches or transports the goods from Switzerland to a foreign destination and the buyer or a third party receives them abroad. This applies to Grade A copper cathodes physically shipped from a Swiss warehouse or Swiss customs-bonded depot, including sales consummated via LME warrant transfer with physical uplift in Switzerland. For goods that never enter Switzerland, the Swiss AG's margin from pure merchanting/transit trade is outside Swiss VAT; the trader must not issue a Swiss VAT invoice or claim export zero-rating for such flows. To preserve 0% VAT and the corresponding input VAT recovery on export-related Swiss costs, the AG must demonstrate the complete logistics chain, the transfer of title/risk abroad, and the receipt of foreign exchange consideration within the statutory substantiation window.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration – electronic export declaration through the Swiss customs processing system (e-dec / NADIM-ES) with the export accompanying document, evidencing physical departure of the copper cathodes from Swiss customs territory.

Bill of Lading – original or certified true copy of the ocean Bill of Lading, CMR waybill, or Air Waybill naming the Swiss AG as consignor and the foreign counterparty as consignee, confirming the foreign discharge port or place of delivery.

Inward Remittance Certificate – SWIFT MT103 or bank certificate evidencing settlement of the invoice by the non-resident buyer; the Swiss exporter must prove receipt of the foreign currency consideration as part of the substantive export proof chain.

Commercial invoice issued by the Swiss AG referencing Art. 23 para. 1 VAT Act, the 0% rate, and the Swiss UID, accompanied by packing list, insurance certificate, warehouse inventory movement report, and LME warrant handover documentation.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV commodity-sector risk program subjects export zero-rating claims to full documentary verification; insufficient substantiation at audit triggers retrospective reclassification at 8.1% VAT plus default interest and denial of related input VAT deductions. Intentional VAT evasion is punishable by a criminal fine of up to four times the evaded tax (Art. 88 VAT Act) with forfeiture of deduction rights; negligent violations carry fines up to CHF 225,000 (Art. 87 VAT Act). Falsified Bills of Lading, phantom exports, and zero-rating claims on goods that never transited Switzerland constitute tax fraud before the Penal Tax Division, leading to damage- and penalty-based clawbacks. The ten-year statutory retention obligation (Art. 96 VAT Act) extends audit exposure; once the 180-day repatriation substantiation period lapses, the ESTV applies evidentiary weight in favor of taxable treatment, and late-produced documentation does not cure the assessment absent force majeure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) is the central bank and monetary authority. There is no dedicated foreign exchange administration or exchange-control authority in Switzerland. Foreign exchange statistics and balance-of-payments monitoring are managed by the SNB; market conduct and banking licensing are supervised by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA); export controls and sanctions implementation are administered by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. The Swiss franc and foreign currencies are freely exchangeable in the interbank and retail markets, with no restriction, approval, registration, or surrender requirement for capital injections, profit repatriation, dividend distribution, trade settlements, or portfolio flows. Profit remittance from a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is available without exchange-control approval, subject to Swiss corporate law solvency tests, statutory audit of annual financial statements, and a 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividends, which may be reduced or refunded under an applicable double tax treaty. Inward and outward foreign direct investments, including share capital increases and shareholder loans, are not subject to SNB licensing. Residents are only required to report selected cross-border asset and liability positions to the SNB for statistical purposes when statutory reporting thresholds are met. Copper cathode trading is treated as a genuine current-account transaction and is freely convertible and transferable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. A Swiss exporter may retain proceeds in any invoicing currency, may convert such proceeds at freely negotiated market rates, and may use them directly for trade disbursements. There is no mandatory surrender of foreign currency to the SNB or any other authority. The only relevant obligation is statistical: resident companies with material foreign receivables, payables, loans, or deposits must report quarterly or annually to the SNB balance-of-payments survey when the SNB notification thresholds are exceeded. Documentary export evidence is nevertheless expected by banks for AML and trade-finance due diligence, including commercial invoices, bills of lading, warehouse receipts, and customs declarations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, subject to FINMA licensing constraints. Switzerland does not recognize an EU e-money or payment-institution passport; a foreign EMI cannot operate autonomously in Switzerland without FINMA authorization. A non-Swiss fintech can offer cross-border clearing to the Swiss entity only through a licensed Swiss bank partner or by obtaining a Swiss fintech banking license or payment services license under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA). The practical route is to use a FINMA-licensed bank as the settlement anchor, with the fintech providing FX and payment-orchestration rails rather than holding client funds independently.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss AML rules and FINMA guidance permit remote onboarding via certified video identification and digital identity verification, provided the bank follows enhanced due diligence and obtains authenticated documents. There is no absolute statutory requirement for directors to appear physically in Switzerland. In practice, for a non-resident-owned Swiss AG engaged in copper cathode trading, the onboarding bank will require at least one recorded video interview with the beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories, together with certified copies of passports, a notarized power of attorney, a Swiss commercial register excerpt, UBO declarations, source of wealth documents, and the trade transaction narrative. The final decision on remote or physical onboarding remains a bank-specific risk decision, and enhanced risk profiles will normally require a physical meeting or a documented video interview with independent verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Copper cathode counterparties in high-risk jurisdictions or featuring sanctioned-adjacent ownership structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening results, LME or COMEX warehouse receipts, final bills of lading, sea-waybills, commercially consistent invoices with Incoterms, chain-of-custody documents, end-user certificates for restricted metals, SWIFT correspondence, and a complete corporate ownership chart for each counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent third-party settlements or unrelated-party payment instructions creating a settlement-risk red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master trading agreements, trade confirmations, dated transaction trail, shipping and customs documents, corresponding MT103 messages, audit-ready flow-of-funds diagrams, bank reference letters, and documentary evidence proving the commercial rationale of each third-party payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership complexity involving trusts, foundations, or bearer-share legacy structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current register of shareholders, articles of association converted to registered shares, trust deeds, foundation charters, UBO declarations with proof of identity, Swiss commercial register excerpt, and legal opinions confirming the source of funds and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disbursements without corresponding physical copper deliveries or documentary evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: LME warrant transfers, warehouse receipts, bills of lading, customs entries via Swiss e-dec, inspection certificates, insurance certificates, transfer deeds, and bank payment confirmations proving the underlying physical shipment or tolerated-delivery mechanism.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the Swiss AG must be routed through SWIFT MT103 or SIC Instant Payment wires from the shareholder bank to the Swiss corporate account using the bank identifier code, the Swiss IBAN, and a clear remittance reference such as 'Kapitalerhöhung', 'Contribution to share capital', or 'Shareholder equity injection'. Switzerland imposes no exchange-control permit and no SNB approval for such flows. For a share capital increase, the notarized shareholders' resolution must be filed in the Swiss commercial register before or contemporaneously with the credited funds. SNB statistical reporting applies only when prescribed balance-of-payments thresholds are exceeded. The receiving Swiss bank must apply standard KYC and may request the corporate resolution, a UBO declaration, and source-of-wealth evidence. For shareholder loans, a documented intercompany loan agreement, arm's-length interest terms, and proper accounting treatment are required; equity must not be disguised as debt for thin-capitalization purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements consist primarily of SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for open-account payments, documentary letters of credit issued through SWIFT MT700 and amended via MT707, standby letters of credit issued via MT760, and SWIFT gpi for end-to-end payment tracking. For copper cathode purchases and sales, settlement may also be executed through the LME clearing systems using LME warrant transfers and warehouse delivery orders. Swiss and European EUR/CHF settling parties can clear through SIC, euroSIC, or SEPA-equivalent channels. Banks also support trade payment undertakings and bank payment obligations in commodity trade finance. All outbound trade disbursements should be backed by the underlying purchase contracts, invoices, logistics documents, and compliance checks against Swiss sanctions regulations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla foreign exchange forwards and forward outrights
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps
FX options, zero-cost collars, strangles, and option combinations

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted or emerging-market currencies, including USD/CNH and other NDF deliverable-in-exception currencies, only where the underlying copper cathode trade is genuine and documented
Currency futures listed on recognized exchanges and cleared through central clearing counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return (Steuererklärung) for federal and cantonal corporate taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung), acting also for Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after close of the fiscal year; extensions available on written request; each canton sets a final calendar date, often 31 May–30 June following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 4%–5% per annum; late-filing penalty of up to CHF 10,000 per cantonal tax law; estimated assessment based on prior year; criminal sanctions for intentional non-disclosure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return (MWST-Abrechnung), where the AG is VAT-registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of every VAT reporting period; annual filing deadline is 60 days after 31 December, unless quarterly filing applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% per annum; administrative penalty up to 10% of tax amount due (maximum CHF 8,000) for procedural violations; fines up to CHF 100,000 for intentional tax evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage and social insurance declaration (AHV/ALV/EO/BVG) where the AG employs staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) and the applicable pension foundation/BVG institution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 January following the calendar year, or by the deadline set by the applicable compensation office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid contributions attract interest at 5% per annum; administrative fines up to CHF 10,000; penal provisions for incomplete or false wage declarations under Art. 87 AHV Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary independent audit required when any two of the following criteria are exceeded in each of two consecutive fiscal years: balance-sheet total > CHF 20 million, annual revenue > CHF 40 million, average 250 full-time employees. Otherwise the AG must perform a limited audit; the shareholders may unanimously waive a limited audit if fewer than 10 employees (Art. 727, 727a CO).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957–963e) prescribes annual financial statements in Swiss accounting principles (Swiss GAAP per OR); listed or consolidated entities may apply Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not require an annual public UBO filing for an ordinary AG. The AG shall maintain a share register (Aktienbuch) and record every transfer of registered shares without delay; if bearer shares are issued, an internal register of beneficial owners must be maintained and made available to authorities upon request. The general meeting or board is not required to file an annual ownership confirmation to the commercial register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share register (Aktienbuch / registre des actions) for registered shares
Minutes of shareholders' general meetings (Minute Book)
Minutes of board of directors' meetings and board resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,500–6,000 (Swiss fiduciary or registered office service with corporate secretarial support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Limited audit: USD 4,000–12,000; ordinary audit: USD 15,000–40,000, depending on turnover and group complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 8.5% federal corporate income tax rate is levied on profit after tax, producing an effective federal burden of 7.83% on pre-tax profit. Combined federal, cantonal and communal effective corporate income tax rates range from approximately 11.9% in Zug to approximately 21.0% in higher-tax urban cantons (Zurich approximately 19.7%). No general statutory tax holidays exist at federal level. Incentives include the mandatory federal patent/IP box (90% exemption on qualifying net IP income), the optional cantonal R&D super-deduction (up to 150% of qualifying R&D expenditure), participation relief providing a 95% exemption on qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from participations of at least 10%, and, for certain new enterprises, temporary cantonal tax relief in some cantons. From 2024, the Swiss Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax applies at 15% to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
